name: Pimosa
tagline: Desktop video, photo, audio & PDF tools.
description:
Pimosa is an offline media utility with more than twenty tools for video, images, GIFs, audio, and PDFs. It is built for practical operations—compressing a recording, converting an image, cropping a clip, merging audio, or rearranging PDF pages—without uploading the material to a web service.

Drop files into the appropriate tool, make the adjustment, and export or batch-process the result. This suits quick production work, web assets, device storage cleanup, and one-off conversions where a full video or image editor would add unnecessary complexity.

Pimosa combines many focused tools rather than being a full non-linear editor. It works offline after installation, but the right outcome still depends on understanding format, resolution, and compression tradeoffs before overwriting or distributing an important original.

## Features

- Compress, convert, resize, crop, merge, rotate, trim, and change the speed of video files.
- Extract audio, convert and merge audio, edit metadata, and create waveform video from audio.
- Compress, convert, resize, crop, flip, rotate, reverse, and create GIFs from image or video material.
- Merge, split, compress, encrypt, crop, rotate, and reorder PDF pages.
- Process media locally without upload limits, work offline after install, and batch-process files on the desktop app.
- Use dedicated simple editors for video trims, social aspect-ratio cropping, image changes, subtitles, and PDF page editing.

## Where it fits

Pimosa fits people who want a single local tool for routine media chores across formats. It can replace a collection of web converters and small, single-purpose editors when speed and privacy matter more than advanced creative control.

It is not a replacement for a professional video-editing suite or a pixel editor. Keep source media when compression or conversion quality must be checked, and review current license terms before deploying it across devices.
